html:
Mysorean rockets were war rockets with iron casings, used by the armies of Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan of Mysore against the British in the late 1700s.

Rockets had been used in India and China for centuries, but with cases of paper or bamboo. Mysore's rockets used a tube of hammered iron. Iron could hold a stronger charge of powder, so the rockets flew farther, up to about two kilometres, and many carried a blade or long bamboo pole. Fired in volleys, they caused panic among cavalry and troops in close order.

They were used in the Anglo Mysore Wars, including at Pollilur in 1780, where the East India Company suffered one of its worst defeats. Tipu kept large rocket units in his army.

After Srirangapatna fell in 1799, the British shipped captured rockets home. William Congreve studied them and built the Congreve rocket, used by Britain in the Napoleonic Wars and in the War of 1812, the "rockets' red glare" of the American anthem. It is a rare case of military technology flowing from India to Europe.
sum: Mysorean rockets were war rockets with iron casings, used by the armies of Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan of Mysore against the British in the late 1700s.
